label: identifier-name-states-role
name: A member, parameter, flag, function or label does not say what it holds or does, contradicts its own comment or behavior, or breaks the surrounding convention
description: What breaks: a reader at the use site cannot tell what the thing is. 'layers' for per-layer K/V HBM bases (2982403509 'pretty non-descript/nebulous'); tok_ix_per_b whose own comment says per-Q (3075717295); 'firstcheck' next to an existing 'first' (2842854014); nk/nh/hs where the code base spells n_kv_heads (2897235803); prepare_hardware_attn_job calling hw_prepare inside launch_hw_attention (3001991780); a function named 'indefinitely' that times out after 4 billion cycles (2380263378 'it's not really waiting forever, right?'); a wrapper split that keeps the old name on the new wrapper (3769684790, withdrawn after seeing the transparent-inheritance reason); a GitHub label 'Benchmark only' beside lower-case 'benchmark' labels (3580238651). Procedure: for every added or renamed identifier compare the name with its trailing comment, with sibling names in the same scope, with the dominant spelling of the same quantity in the repository and with what the body does; for names that state a phase or behavior (prepare, launch, indefinitely, traced) check the body honors it. Severity nit to minor; suggestion blocks for one-word renames.
disposition_reason: Check 13 covers only value-suffixed constant stems; members, parameters, flags, functions and labels need a name-vs-comment and name-vs-sibling procedure of their own. 8 rows over 7 PRs.
agent_feasibility: yes: name-vs-comment and name-vs-sibling comparisons are mechanical; whether 'indefinitely' misleads (2380263378) needs the mwaitx operand semantics.

members.concern: The new struct member `layers` (a per-layer vector of K/V HBM bases in struct shard) has a name too generic to tell a reader what it holds; he asks for `kv_shard_layers`.

detection.trigger: A diff adds or renames a member, variable or parameter whose name is a bare generic noun (layers, data, items, list, vals) while the removed names or the trailing comment carry the specific meaning (k_base/v_base, 'k/v HBM bases').
detection.procedure: For each added declaration in a header, compare the identifier against the comment on the same line and the names it replaces; grep the enclosing struct for other members or constructor parameters that share the word (here the constructor takes a `layers` count parameter).
detection.question: Would a reader at a use site know from the identifier alone what the member holds, without the comment?

members.quote: I would prefer something like `kv_shard_layers`? Just 'layers' is pretty non-descript/nebulous
members.note: Head af9438799a: h/tron/shard.hpp:37 member is `kv_shard_layers`. Author added that `layer` is also a constructor parameter (shard::shard(PosDevice*, uint32_t base, uint32_t layers)), so the generic name collided with a parameter name.

members.concern: The new field tok_ix_per_b (per-query token indices in the device work-queue entry wqentry) uses the opaque letter 'b'/'B' (the MAX_B family in h/tron/gof.hpp) while its own comment says 'per-Q'; Wade asks why it is not named tok_ix_per_q to match what it is and how it is documented.

detection.trigger: The diff adds or renames a field, parameter or constant whose identifier carries a one-letter or abbreviation token (b, B, n, x, tmp) while the trailing comment or doc on the same line names the concept with a different full word (per-Q, query, token).
detection.procedure: For each added declaration with a trailing comment, split the identifier into tokens and compare them with the nouns in the comment; flag when the comment's noun (query/Q) is absent from the identifier and the identifier's distinguishing token is a single letter. Grep h/ for the letter family (`git grep -n 'MAX_B\b' HEAD -- h`) to see whether the opaque name is an inherited convention; the ask is still to name the new field by its documented role.
detection.question: Reading only the identifier at a use site, can a reader tell what it indexes, and does the field's own comment use a different word than the name?

members.quote: I've never understood this magic '`b`'/'`B`' nomenclature we use... why can't we call this `tok_ix_per_q` instead, which is exactly what it is, and literally how it's documented?
members.note: Verified at head 1a88e897e1: h/pos/device.hpp:85 still declares `std::array<size_t, tron::hardware::MAX_B> tok_ix_per_b{};  // per-Q token indices`, and MAX_B is used for results/activations/shards/nanlocations arrays in the same header (lines 60, 61, 92, 138), so 'B' is a pre-existing batch-dimension convention from gof.hpp. No reply from the author. Check 13 shares the theme (a name must state its role, not an opaque token) but its trigger is the value-suffix constant family, so it would not fire on a struct field; a widened 'role-bearing names' check that covers fields and parameters with a comment-vs-identifier mismatch would. Severity minor is inferred: no 'nit' word, phrased as a question, no blocking language.

members.concern: Wade asks to rename the new flag `firstcheck` to `first_tsccheck` so its name says which check it gates, since the same function already has a flag named `first` for a different purpose.

detection.trigger: A hunk adds a boolean or counter whose name is generic (`first`, `firstcheck`, `done`, `flag`) next to an existing variable with a near-identical name in the same scope.
detection.procedure: Read the enclosing function at the comment's commit; list every local whose name shares the stem (here `first` at driver.cpp:910 gates the one-time 'saw wait time' log, `firstcheck` at :911 gates check_for_tsc_errs). If two locals share a stem and gate different things, propose a name that names the gated thing, as a ```suggestion block.
detection.question: Reading only the use site, can a reader tell which event this flag is the first of?

members.note: Read at commit 021072570b: `bool first = true;` (line 910) and `bool firstcheck = true;` (line 911) in wait_for_xfer_blocks; `first` guards the one-time 'DMA XFER saw wait time' debug log, `firstcheck` guards check_for_tsc_errs. Author's follow-up commit b1c1523c27 'integrate review feedback' renamed it to `firsttsccheck` (no underscore; gh pr diff 2103 lines 'bool firsttsccheck = true;'), not Wade's exact spelling. The same PR also adds a `first` flag in readback_check with the same gating role and Wade did not comment on that one. Check 13 fit is partial: check 13 keys on value-suffixed constants; the shared theme is 'name must carry the role'.

members.concern: The parameters of gof_configure are abbreviated (nk, nh, hs) while the rest of the code base spells them n_kv_heads, n_heads, head_size; Wade offers a suggestion block with the full names.

detection.trigger: A diff adds a function signature whose parameter names are two-letter abbreviations (nk, nh, hs, sh) for quantities that have an established spelled-out name elsewhere.
detection.procedure: For each abbreviated parameter, grep h/ and src/ for the spelled-out form (n_kv_heads, n_heads, head_size) and count hits. If the long form dominates, propose the rename as a suggestion block; mark it nit.
detection.question: Does the code base already have a dominant spelling for this quantity, and does the new signature deviate from it?

members.quote: a bit of a nit, but I prefer to see more descriptive param names ;)... and would be consistent with naming conventions elsewhere
members.note: Author applied it in de3bb7c7 (commit subject 'use descriptive parameter names for gof_configure'). The call site at model.hpp:761 already passed variables named n_kv_heads, n_heads, head_size, so the inconsistency was visible from the PR's own diff. Skill section 'How Wade words a finding' says he does not comment on the C++ guide; this naming nit is an exception that the skill does not cover.

members.concern: Nit on naming/layering: `prepare_hardware_attn_job` calls `hw_prepare`, both inside the `launch_hw_attention` path, which blurs prepare vs launch; he asks how much of this will be reshaped by Bill's scheduler work before investing in it.

detection.trigger: A diff adds a call whose name says one phase (prepare) inside a function whose name says another phase (launch), or nests two functions with the same phase word.
detection.procedure: Read the call chain the hunk sits in (launch_hw_attention -> prepare_hardware_attn_job -> hw_prepare); list the phase words in each name; check the PR body or linked issues for a planned refactor that would move this code.
detection.question: Does the function name describe the phase in which the call actually runs, and is a known upcoming change going to move it anyway?

members.quote: definitely a nit, but now we have **prepare**\_hardware\_blah, which calls hw\_**prepare**, both in the **launch**\_hw path. How much of this will get modified/moved around by the time we have Bill's work?
members.note: Needs knowledge of Bill's pending scheduler work (team plan, not in repo). Author deferred to Bill. Wade explicitly labels severity 'definitely a nit'.

members.concern: The function is named 'indefinitely' but it uses mwaitx with a timeout operand of 0xFFFFFFFF cycles, so each wait wakes after about 4 billion cycles rather than waiting forever; Wade asks whether a true indefinite wait would use mwait instead and whether the name is misleading.

detection.trigger: A hunk changes the body of a function whose name states a behavior (indefinitely, never, always, once, untraced) and the new body contains an operand, comment or branch that contradicts the name (here `options = 2; // Use timeout` next to `"b"(0xFFFFFFFF)); // No timeout`).
detection.procedure: Read the function body at HEAD; list each statement that bounds or conditions the behavior the name promises (a timeout operand, a loop bound, a capability check); for ISA operands, check the instruction reference (AMD mwaitx: ECX bit 1 enables the EBX timeout in TSC cycles); state whether the outer loop restores the promised behavior; then ask whether the name or the body should change.
detection.question: Does the function, as a whole, do what its name says, and if only because an outer loop re-enters, does the inline comment say so?

members.quote: this function is named "indefinitely" but it's not _really_ waiting forever, right? A true indefinite wait would use "mwait" instead of "mwaitx", correct? This method is instead basically waiting 4 billion cycles, and then will time-out anyway
members.note: Code fact at 08b5f10085 src/pos/mwaitx.cpp:69-85: `static void indefinitely(volatile uint64_t* trigger, auto condition)` loops `while (!condition(*trigger))`; inside, when MWAITX_SUPPORTED, it executes monitorx then `uint32_t options = 2; // Use timeout` and `mwaitx` with `"c"(options), "b"(0xFFFFFFFF)); // No timeout`. The two comments contradict each other on the same instruction. Because the outer while loop re-enters after each wake, the function does wait until the condition holds (indefinite as a whole), but each mwaitx sleep is bounded at 2^32 TSC cycles (about 1 to 2 s at 2 to 4 GHz). Wade's claim that it 'will time-out anyway' is right per instruction and wrong per function. Also, when MWAITX_SUPPORTED is false (the Granite Rapids case this PR is for), the loop is a pure busy spin. Addressed to @BillBaumann, not the PR author, and framed as a learning question ('newby-probe here :)'). PR closed unmerged; no reply.

members.concern: When a function (drain_reserves, the slab-cache drain in the DMA heap) is split into a traced wrapper and an untraced core, Wade thinks the original name should stay on the original body and the new wrapper should carry the new name (drain_reserved_traced), not the other way round.

detection.trigger: A hunk renames an existing function body to a `_untraced`/`_impl`/`_inner` variant and gives the original name to a new thin wrapper that adds instrumentation (TRACE_EVENT, logging, a counter).
detection.procedure: Read the hunk; list the callers of the original name (grep h/ src/ t/ for `drain_reserves(`); check whether the PR body states that existing callers should inherit the instrumentation; if it does, the direction is deliberate and the finding is at most a naming note; if not, ask which direction was intended.
detection.question: Should existing callers of the original name receive the new instrumentation transparently (keep the name on the wrapper), or opt in (new name on the wrapper)?

members.quote: IMHO, the new function should have been named `drain_reserved_traced()` and the original left as-is, where `_traced` variant wraps the original `drain_reserves()`
members.note: Wade retracted this seven minutes later in inline 3769729340 after reading the private declaration in h/system/heap_v2.hpp:416. Code fact at 22b5e0d59c: src/system/heap_v2.cpp has `uint32_t pos_heap_v2::drain_reserves_untraced() noexcept` (the old body, now returning a released-slab count) and `void pos_heap_v2::drain_reserves() noexcept` wrapping it in TRACE_EVENT_BEGIN/END on the 'memory' category. No code change followed.

members.concern: The new label that triggers the workflow is spelled 'Benchmark only' while the repository's existing benchmark labels use a lower-case 'b'; Wade asks for a consistent lower-case name, 'dev-benchmark-only'.

detection.trigger: The diff introduces a new user-facing name that selects behavior (a GitHub label string in a workflow `if:` or `contains(labels.*.name, ...)` expression, an env var, a CMake option, a CLI flag) in a file that has sibling files defining names of the same kind.
detection.procedure: Collect the sibling names of the same kind: grep `labels.*.name` and `label.name` across .github/workflows at BASE (here: 'Run CI', 'Continuous integration'), and the repository label list (`gh label list`). Compare casing, separator and prefix style of the new name against those. Also check the same name is spelled identically at every use site in the new file (the trigger block, the concurrency group and the job `if:`).
detection.question: Does the new name follow the casing and word-separator style of the existing names of the same kind in the repository, and if not, is there a stated reason?

members.quote: just a trivial nit: our current `benchmark` labels use lower-case 'b'. Maybe it would be more intuitive if we made this label `dev-benchmark-only`?
members.note: At the reviewed commit the workflow used the label 'Benchmark only' (line 34 `contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'Benchmark only')`). At the merged head 57368de081 every site says 'dev-benchmark-only' (lines 6, 16, 34, 36). The sibling workflows at BASE gate on the labels 'Run CI' (cmake-single-platform.yml:171, nix-build.yml:37) and 'Continuous integration' (test-release-build.yml:16); the lower-case `benchmark` labels Wade cites are repository labels, not visible in the workflow files (Insufficient data in the worktree: `gh label list` would confirm). Wade is one of the two allowlisted authors of this workflow, so the name is one he will type. He approved one minute later without waiting for the rename.

codex_bullets.bullet: Do not accept an unbounded wait as proof that a race is fixed. Identify the event that ends the wait and whether the failure being handled prevents that event. Preserve actionable diagnostics.
codex_bullets.reason: Three comments (PRs 2872, 2766, 1485). 3342904643 carries a Claude-summarized block but the position ("I loathe spin-waits", "there's more sleuthing to be done") is Wade's own. No Claude check.

codex_bullets.bullet: Follow current repository and user conventions. Wade's naming and formatting preferences are usually nits. His later acceptance of value suffixes in established kernel code does not prescribe them for shared code.
codex_bullets.reason: Five comments (PRs 4557, 2089, 2287, 2011); naming nits are frequent (also 2982403509, 2941290531). The corpus shows Wade did raise the suffix for shared code; the Claude skill should narrow "never a finding" to the author's kernel files.
codex_bullets.claude_skill_coverage: partial (check 13 covers stems; it declares the value suffix "never a finding", which 6021333114 contradicts for shared code)
